alerts.title: Abdominal pain: ADR screening and reporting required
alerts.message: Guidelines require all healthcare workers to screen for suspected adverse drug reactions at each encounter using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs should be recorded and reported. The patient reports new abdominal pain today, but the clinician's plan does not document formal ADR screening or submit an aDSM form. Abdominal pain could relate to TDF-associated nephrotoxicity or hepatotoxicity, though the patient's appetite is preserved and no fever is noted, arguing against acute infection or severe hepatobiliary disease.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the Drug Safety Screening checklist for abdominal pain, document findings in the ART card or eMRS, and submit an aDSM form if an ADR is suspected.
